| Maximum basic rate | $1,135.40 | $855.90 | $1,711.80 |
| Maximum Pension Supplement | $88.20 | $66.50 | $133.00 |
| Energy Supplement | $14.10 | $10.60 | $21.20 |
| **Increase per fortnight** | $36.80 | $27.80 | $55.60 |
| **Increase per year** | $956.80 | $722.80 | $1,445.60 |

### **Deeming rates from 20 September 2026**
For the third time in the past year, the government is increasing deeming rates.

From 20 September 2026, the deeming rate will increase from 1.25 per cent to 1.75 per cent for financial assets up to $66,800 for singles and $110,600 for couples combined. For all financial assets exceeding the threshold, the rate has risen by 0.5 per cent to 3.75 per cent.

|  |  |  |
|-|-|-|
| **Asset threshold** | **New rate** | **Previous rate** |
| First $66,800 (single) / $110,600 (couple) | 1.75% | 1.25% |
| Assets above the threshold | 3.75% | 3.25% |

# Deeming rate recommendation – March 2026
## New rates
- 1.25% for financial assets below the threshold
- 3.25% for financial assets above the threshold

## Why the rates are changing
The updated rates reflect investment returns that are available to the majority of payment recipients.

They also support the government's plan to gradually reset the deeming rates after the rate freeze ended on 30 June 2025.

results.title: Deeming rates and calculator for the Age Pension income test
results.description:
# Deeming rates and calculator for the Age Pension income test
In recent years, deeming rates shifted from being an arcane concept few people knew or cared about, to a hot button issue for retirees struggling to make ends meet at a time of rising interest rates and cost-of-living pressures.

## What are the current deeming rates?
| Situation | Deeming lower rate | Deeming higher rate |
|-|-|-|
| **Single** | 1.75% on the first **$66,800** of your investment assets, plus | 3.75% on your investment assets over the amount of **$66,800** |
| **Couple** | 1.75% on the first **$110,600** of your combined investment assets, plus | 3.75% on your combined investment assets over the amount of **$110,600** |

## Deeming rates and thresholds: current and previous periods
Deeming rates have moved five times since 2019, with a long freeze in the middle.

Before 1 July 2019, the rates were 1.75% (lower) and 3.25% (higher). Retirees were then earning less on their bank deposits than they were deemed to earn, and the resulting pressure led the federal government to cut the rates twice: to 1% and 3% from 1 July 2019, and to 0.25% and 2.25% from 1 May 2020.

Since then the rates have stepped back up three times: to 0.75% and 2.75% from 20 September 2025, to 1.25% and 3.25% from 20 March 2026, and to 1.75% and 3.75% from 20 September 2026.

The Reserve Bank of Australia left the cash rate at 4.35% at its meeting on 11 August 2026, while the higher deeming rate is 3.75%.

The higher deeming rate fell from 3.25% to 2.25%, was frozen until September 2025, and rises to 3.75% on 20 September 2026. The lower deeming rate fell from 1.75% to 0.25% and rises to 1.75%. The RBA cash rate fell from 1.5% to 0.1% by November 2020, rose to 4.35% by November 2023, dipped to 3.6% during 2025 and returned to 4.35% in May 2026.
